answer: Continuous work attestation. Each identity must submit periodic proof of having solved a unique, verifiable computation tied to its own history; the latest proof becomes a vertex in a chain only that identity can extend. Replaying another identity's work yields a detectable collision, so copying costs a full recomputation. A relic from any prior epoch must be re-earned, and the crystal of accumulated proofs cannot be forged without redoing all prior labor. Cloning thus costs the entire compute history per identity, making honest participation cheaper than running duplicates.
